# google_storage_control_feature_config

A feature configuration resource for Google Cloud Storage Control.
FeatureConfig manages Smart Storage features such as Auto Annotate (Object enrichments) within a given project. Auto Annotate uses AI models (such as label detection, object detection, etc.) to analyze and enrich Google Cloud Storage objects.


To get more information about FeatureConfig, see:

* [API documentation](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/reference/rest/storage/v2/projects.locations.featureConfigs)
* How-to Guides
    * [Cloud Storage Control Overview](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/overview-storage-control)

## Example Usage - Storage Control Feature Config Basic


```hcl
resource "google_storage_bucket" "test_bucket" {
  name     = "example-bkt"
  location = "US"
}

resource "google_storage_control_feature_config" "example" {
  feature_config_id = "example-fc"
  description       = "Basic feature config for Auto Annotate"
  filter {
    included_cloud_storage_buckets {
      bucket_id_regexes = [google_storage_bucket.test_bucket.name]
    }
  }
  auto_annotate_config {
    processing_location = "us"
    models {
      name = "label-detector"
    }
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `auto_annotate_config` -
  (Required)
  Configuration for auto_annotate (Object enrichments).
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_auto_annotate_config).

* `feature_config_id` -
  (Required)
  The ID to use for the feature config, which will become the final component of the feature config's resource name.


* `description` -
  (Optional)
  A description of the feature configuration.

* `filter` -
  (Optional)
  Filter over location and bucket using include or exclude semantics.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_filter).

* `location` -
  (Optional)
  Resource ID segment making up resource `name`. It identifies the resource within its parent collection.
  Currently, only `global` is supported.

* `project` - (Optional) The ID of the project in which the resource belongs.
    If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

* `deletion_policy` - (Optional) Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the resource. Defaults to DELETE.
	When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the resource,
	the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
	When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
	management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
	When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.


<a name="nested_auto_annotate_config"></a>The `auto_annotate_config` block supports:

* `processing_location` -
  (Required)
  Specifies the geographic location (case-sensitive) where data is processed.
  Currently, only multi-regional locations such as `us`, `eu`, or `asia` are supported.
  To avoid duplicate billing, it is highly recommended to configure exactly one processing location
  per bucket and model combination. If you configure multiple processing locations for the same
  bucket and model across different configurations, the system triggers separate annotation runs in
  each location, and you will be billed for every resulting annotation.

* `models` -
  (Required)
  The list of unique models selected. Each model is uniquely identified by its `name` string.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_auto_annotate_config_models).


<a name="nested_auto_annotate_config_models"></a>The `models` block supports:

* `name` -
  (Required)
  The name of the model (for example, `label-detector`, `object-detector`).

<a name="nested_filter"></a>The `filter` block supports:

* `included_cloud_storage_buckets` -
  (Optional)
  Buckets to include.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_filter_included_cloud_storage_buckets).


<a name="nested_filter_included_cloud_storage_buckets"></a>The `included_cloud_storage_buckets` block supports:

* `bucket_id_regexes` -
  (Required)
  List of Cloud Storage buckets to include. Note that Auto Annotate requires exact bucket names rather than regular expression patterns.

## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/featureConfigs/{{feature_config_id}}`

* `name` -
  The name of the FeatureConfig resource.

* `create_time` -
  The time at which the feature configuration was created.

* `update_time` -
  The time at which the feature configuration was last updated.

* `type` -
  Specifies the type of the feature configuration.


## Timeouts

This resource provides the following
[Timeouts](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/sdkv2/resources/retries-and-customizable-timeouts) configuration options:

- `create` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `update` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `delete` - Default is 20 minutes.

## Import


FeatureConfig can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/featureConfigs/{{feature_config_id}}`
* `{{project}}/{{location}}/{{feature_config_id}}`
* `{{location}}/{{feature_config_id}}`

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`identity` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/import#identity) to import FeatureConfig using identity values. For example:

```tf
import {
  identity = {
    location = "<-optional value->"
    featureConfigId = "<-required value->"
    project = "<-optional value->"
  }
  to = google_storage_control_feature_config.default
}
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import FeatureConfig using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/featureConfigs/{{feature_config_id}}"
  to = google_storage_control_feature_config.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), FeatureConfig can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_storage_control_feature_config.default projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/featureConfigs/{{feature_config_id}}
$ terraform import google_storage_control_feature_config.default {{project}}/{{location}}/{{feature_config_id}}
$ terraform import google_storage_control_feature_config.default {{location}}/{{feature_config_id}}
```
